pairs.why: B's driving wheels sit on the rails and line up with the track angle, while A's small front wheels and big cowcatcher plate hang off the line of the rails.
A's X-legs, armrests and seat all hold together as one folding frame, while B's front seat bar sticks out past the frame and is not clearly joined to the legs or the back.
B's dome, rim lights and underside are all seen from one slightly low eye level, while A's disc is seen from high above and its dome is seen almost side-on.
A's lifebuoy hangs from a post by a cord and the deck rests on its pilings, while B's lifebuoy reflection appears far below and away from where the ring actually is.

A's four wheels and front tongue follow one camera and carry the box, while B's tongue comes out of the side of the box and slants down to the ground, and its single front wheel can't carry the wagon.
A's lifebuoy, rope and posts are attached and all seen from one camera, while B's lifebuoy reflection sits far away from the ring.
B's checkerboard top, pedestal and stools are all seen from one consistent high angle, while A's tabletop looks turned and tilted compared with its pedestal base.
B's locomotive runs along the same diagonal as its track, while A's body is turned three-quarters toward the viewer but sits on rails that run flat across the picture.
